groups.title: Server information
groups.description: Identify a server and check whether it is ready. Players and monitoring tools can read the public checks before signing in.

groups.title: Sign-in and profiles
groups.description: Sign people in with local credentials or a TV code, select a profile and renew the session. These flows are for player apps; API keys and personal access tokens cannot replace a session on session-only routes.

groups.title: Keys and personal access tokens
groups.description: Let a signed-in member create a scoped credential for a script or integration. Credential management requires a session, even when the caller already has an admin-scoped key.

groups.title: Browse and search
groups.description: Find visible libraries and titles, or build a player screen from the server’s published browse choices. Structured browse keeps filtering, ordering and access checks on the server. A movie, episode or track is a title in the app; the API calls these `items`.

groups.title: Title details and artwork
groups.description: Read title details, episode and track order, credits and images. These reads apply the viewer’s current library access and content restrictions.

groups.title: Playback sessions
groups.description: Publish the player’s real capabilities, request a presentation and report what the renderer does. Session revisions and leases keep controls and progress consistent.

groups.title: Playback queues
groups.description: Build and edit a device queue without loading all its entries. Queue revisions protect edits, and audio players can prepare the next entry before the current one ends.

groups.title: Media and subtitles
groups.description: Fetch media and subtitle resources using the URLs in a playback presentation. Grant-bearing URLs still enforce session and viewer access; clients should not construct them.

groups.title: Offline downloads
groups.description: Prepare media, transfer its companion files and retain signed permission for offline playback. Download-capable players also revalidate receipts and reconcile progress when they reconnect.

groups.title: Personal state and bulk jobs
groups.description: Read and change the current profile’s watched state, My List, favourites, history and preferences. Bulk jobs capture a selection and report progress and individual failures.

groups.title: Playlists and saved lists
groups.description: Create and edit playlists, personal collections and saved filters. Revisions and operation IDs protect list edits, and sharing remains subject to the caller’s access.

groups.title: Live TV and recordings
groups.description: Read the TV guide, play channels and manage the current viewer’s recordings. Source setup, tuner administration and storage policy belong to the server owner’s console.

groups.title: Events and notifications
groups.description: Keep open clients current with invalidation hints and a paged notification inbox. Event positions and inbox revisions are separate values.

groups.title: Title queries and scans
groups.description: Let catalogue indexes and download managers find titles and notify Portico about changed files. Scan and path-reporting writes require an owner’s credential with library scope.

groups.title: Metadata integrations
groups.description: Inspect and repair title matches or update metadata through an owner-authorized integration. These operations use library scope and keep revision checks separate from background provider work.

groups.title: Playback dashboards and controls
groups.description: Show active playback and let an authorized administrator control it. Admin scope and the administrator’s playback permission are both required.

groups.title: Webhooks
groups.description: Send signed event notifications to automation services and other integrations. An owner can manage subscriptions and inspect delivery results with an admin-scoped credential.

groups.title: AI assistants with MCP
groups.description: Connect an assistant to the server with a deliberately scoped API key or personal access token. The tool list follows both the credential’s scopes and the member’s current permissions.

operations.title: Read server information
operations.description: Identify the server before signing in, using its ID, name, version and setup status.

operations.title: Read server identity and API version
operations.description: Read the server ID, name, setup status and API version. `major` identifies the API major version; `level` is the numeric API level within that version, currently 1. Use these values when checking client compatibility.

operations.title: Read server liveness
operations.description: Check liveness with a small response that excludes account and dependency details. Monitoring tools can use it without credentials.

operations.title: Read database readiness
operations.description: Checks that the database responds and returns 503 when the server is not ready. Use this for an external readiness probe.

operations.title: Read the server's readiness state
operations.description: Check the readiness flag and status, including starting or degraded states. A 503 response includes Retry-After.

operations.title: Read available features and limits
operations.description: Check feature states and published limits for the current profile. Use it to decide which client features to offer.

operations.title: Read available sign-in methods
operations.description: Check which sign-in methods and policies this server supports. Read it before offering a local sign-in or pairing option.

operations.title: Sign in with local credentials
operations.description: Signs in with a username and password and returns the account snapshot and session after the server accepts the sign-in. Handle a two-factor challenge, required password change, pending device approval or account-only session before browsing.

params.X-Portico-Installation-Id: Stable random ID for this installation, 32–128 letters, digits, hyphens or underscores.

notes: Persist a random installation ID and send X-Portico-Installation-Id and the device/app headers.
Tokenless cross-origin browser sign-in is refused; native clients can omit Origin.
Local credentials and TV codes are the documented third-party sign-in paths; third-party Portico Account assertion issuance is not provided.
operations.auth: Send sign-in credentials in the request body; API keys and personal access tokens are refused.

operations.title: Complete a two-factor challenge
operations.description: Submits the challenge token and current verification code from sign-in. Success returns the sign-in result after the second factor is proven.
operations.auth: Send the challenge token and verification code in the request body; API keys and personal access tokens are refused.

operations.title: Read the account and its profiles
operations.description: Read the signed-in account snapshot and its available profiles. An account-only session can use this to reach profile selection.

operations.title: Select a profile
operations.description: Selects a profile with its PIN or remembered trust token where required and returns new session credentials. Remembered trust belongs to the same installation.
notes: Save the replacement session credentials before issuing viewer requests.

operations.title: End the outgoing profile's sessions
operations.description: Revokes the outgoing profile's session families on the named installation before another profile takes over. This also ends their playback and queues on that device.
notes: Keep usable account credentials for selecting the next profile; the outgoing families are revoked.

operations.title: Change the local account password
operations.description: Changes the password after proving the current password and any required second factor. Use it to complete a required password change, then sign in again because existing sessions end.

operations.title: Renew a session
operations.description: Exchanges the refresh token for a new session envelope bound to the installation. Save both tokens atomically and retry a lost response with the same refresh token, installation ID and request ID.
notes: Store refresh tokens privately and serialize refreshes within the app. Reusing a predecessor outside an exact retry can revoke its session family.
operations.auth: Send the refresh token, installationId and requestId in the request body; API keys and personal access tokens are refused.

operations.title: Read the current member and profile
operations.description: Identify the authenticated member and selected profile, with their permissions. Use it after profile selection to establish whose state the app is showing.

operations.title: Read a profile picture
operations.description: Fetch a profile's avatar image subject to access checks. Use the returned avatar URL when displaying the profile picker.

params.id: Profile ID from the account’s profile list.
params.v: Avatar version from the returned URL.

operations.title: Sign out this session
operations.description: Revokes the entire current session family, including its playback access. It accepts an authentic expired or retired family token and takes no query or body.
operations.auth: Send a session-family access token in Authorization; authentic expired or retired tokens are accepted, but API keys and personal access tokens are refused.

operations.title: Request a TV sign-in code
operations.description: Creates a pairing attempt and returns the display code, verification URLs, expiry and polling interval. Keep deviceCode private and show the returned verification address.
notes: Persist a random installation ID and send X-Portico-Installation-Id and the device/app headers.
Tokenless cross-origin browser sign-in is refused; native clients can omit Origin.

operations.title: Review a TV sign-in request
operations.description: Looks up a user code so the signed-in member can inspect the waiting device before deciding. This step does not approve it.

operations.title: Approve or deny a TV sign-in
operations.description: Records the signed-in member's decision for a user code and returns 204. An approved device receives the approver's identity and role, including owner authority when the owner approves.

operations.title: Collect the TV session
operations.description: Polls a pairing attempt with its secret device code and returns the session envelope after approval. Honour the polling interval and Retry-After for authorization_pending or slow_down, and stop on denial or expiry.
operations.auth: The secret deviceCode in the request body authorizes polling; API keys and personal access tokens are refused.

operations.title: Cancel a TV sign-in request
operations.description: Cancels an unused pairing attempt with its device code. Call it when the viewer leaves the waiting screen.
operations.auth: The secret deviceCode in the request body authorizes cancellation; API keys and personal access tokens are refused.

operations.title: Read credential options and limits
operations.description: Check available scopes, credential limits and whether members may create personal access tokens. Read this before presenting a credential form.

operations.title: List your personal access tokens
operations.description: Lists the current member's personal access tokens with hints, usage and lifecycle state. Stored secrets cannot be read back.

params.cursor: Continuation returned by the previous page; send it unchanged with the same query.
params.limit: Credentials per page, 1–100; defaults to 25.

operations.title: Create a personal access token
operations.description: Creates a personal access token for the signed-in member with the requested scopes and optional expiry. The client-generated `operationId` in the request body prevents duplicate creation, but a replay does not return the secret again. Save the secret from the first successful response.
notes: Reuse the client-generated `operationId` in the request body only when retrying the same request; use a new value for a new request.

operations.title: Revoke a personal access token
operations.description: Revokes one of the current member's personal access tokens and takes effect on its next request. Revocation is safe to repeat.

operations.title: List server API keys
operations.description: Lets the owner list integration keys, including their scopes, usage and state. The list shows secret hints rather than full secrets.

params.cursor: Continuation returned by the previous page; send it unchanged with the same query.
params.limit: Credentials per page, 1–100; defaults to 25.

operations.title: Create an API key
operations.description: Lets a signed-in owner create a scoped integration key with an optional expiry. Save the secret from the first successful response; replaying the client-generated `operationId` in the request body does not reveal it again.
notes: Reuse the client-generated `operationId` in the request body only when retrying the same request; use a new value for a new request.

operations.title: Revoke an API key
operations.description: Lets a signed-in owner revoke an integration key. The key stops working on its next request and the revocation is safe to repeat.

operations.title: List visible libraries
operations.description: Find the libraries available to the current profile and their default views. Use their IDs for browsing and title queries.

operations.title: Read Home
operations.description: Build the current profile's Home screen from its hero, layout and initial rows. Continue individual rows through their returned paging information.

params.limit: Initial entries per Home row, 1–60; defaults to 12. Larger values are capped at 60.

operations.title: Read more of a Home row
operations.description: Continue one Home row with a bounded portion of its entries. Use its cursor or positional window with the matching revision rather than loading the whole library.

params.id: Home row ID from the Home response.
params.limit: Entries per row window, 1–60; defaults to 12. Larger values are capped at 60.
params.cursor: Continuation returned by the previous page; send it unchanged with the same query.
params.start: Starting row position; use the revision belonging to this row.
params.revision: Revision from the same Home row being continued.
params.anchorId: Entry ID used to anchor the requested row window.

operations.title: Read a Saved screen
operations.description: Read the Saved screen named by `view`, with its headings, sections, navigation, sorts and filters. Use the returned choices for the current profile’s Saved content.

params.sort: For `watchlist` and `favorites`: title (default), added, updated, year, duration or progress. For `playlists`: title (default), created, updated or count.
params.direction: asc or desc. Defaults to asc for `watchlist` and `favorites`. For `playlists`, defaults to asc for title and desc for created, updated and count.
params.filter: For `watchlist` and `favorites`: all (default), unwatched or inProgress. For `playlists`: all (default), mine, shared or pinned.
params.limit: Entries per page, 1–100; defaults to 40.
params.cursor: Continuation returned by the previous page; send it unchanged with the same query.

operations.title: Read a library screen
operations.description: Build a library screen with navigation, sections, available sorts and filters. The view and entityId select the library or subgroup being shown.

params.view: Video libraries: discover, browse, collections, categories, collection, show or season. Music: browse, discover, releases, songs, artist, album or disc. Audiobooks: browse, discover, authors, series, author, book or book_series. Use the navigation returned for the library. Defaults to discover for movies and browse for other library kinds.
params.entityId: Entity ID selecting a subgroup within the requested content view.
params.sort: Video browse and collection views: title (default), plus added or year for movies. Collections and artist views use title. Other video views use server (discover), decade (categories), season (show) or episode (season). Music and audiobook views use title, track (album/disc), part (book), order (book_series) or server (discover).
params.direction: asc or desc for title, added and year. Defaults to desc for added, year and decade; otherwise asc. Video discover requires asc and categories requires desc. Ordered show, season, album, disc, book and book_series views require asc.
params.category: Movie category ID from the returned filters; accepted only with browse or collection.
params.q: Title prefix, at most 100 bytes; omit for discover and ordered show, season, album, disc, book and book_series views, and for video categories.
params.cursor: Continuation returned by the previous page; send it unchanged with the same query.
params.limit: Entries per page, 1–100; defaults to 40. Larger values are capped at 100.
params.start: Zero-based nonnegative starting position; defaults to 0. A positive start is accepted for video browse, collection, collections or artist views, without cursor; music and audiobook views ignore it.
params.section: Listed in the spec but unused by this handler. Continue a section with its returned cursor.

operations.title: Read library browse options
operations.description: Discover this library's supported fields, operators, pivots, sorts and query limits. Read it before building a structured browse request.

params.pivot: Movie: discover, movies, collections or categories. TV/anime: discover, shows, episodes, collections or categories. Music: discover, artists, albums, songs or genres. Audiobooks: discover, authors, books or series. Omit to read the library’s full vocabulary.

operations.title: List library facet values
operations.description: Find values and counts for a supported browse field within the visible library. Use q to narrow the facet choices.

params.field: Counted facet field: genre, decade, year, contentRating, resolution, audioLanguage, studio, network, tag, label, series or collection.
params.q: Optional text to filter facet values, at most 100 bytes.
params.limit: Facet values, 1–200; defaults to 200. Larger values are capped at 200.

operations.title: Browse a library
operations.description: Runs a structured filter and sort over visible library entries. Continue with pageInfo.nextCursor or use a positional range with its revision; totals above 10,000 are reported as a lower bound.
notes: Read browse capabilities first. Keep cursors and positional revisions with the query and viewer that produced them.

operations.title: Read cross-library browse options
operations.description: Discover supported fields, pivots, sorts and limits for grouped lists across visible libraries. Use it before browsing a person, playlist or personal list.

operations.title: List cross-library facet values
operations.description: Find facet choices and counts across the current profile's libraries. Group and value can restrict the facet to the same group as the browse query.

params.field: Counted facet field: genre, decade, year, contentRating, resolution, audioLanguage, studio, network, tag, label, series or collection.
params.q: Optional text to filter facet values, at most 100 bytes.
params.limit: Facet values, 1–200; defaults to 200. Larger values are capped at 200.
params.group: Optional group, such as a person’s credits (`person`, `cast` or `crew`), a playlist (`list`), a personal collection (`savedCollection`), a Home row (`homeRow`), My List (`watchlisted`), favourites (`favorite`) or History (`lastPlayedAt`).
params.value: Person ID for `person`, `cast` or `crew`; playlist ID for `list`; personal collection ID for `savedCollection`; Home row ID for `homeRow`. Ignored for My List (`watchlisted`), favourites (`favorite`) and History (`lastPlayedAt`).

operations.title: Browse a group across libraries
operations.description: Runs a structured query for a named group such as a person, playlist, Home row, My List or History. Results are paged and preserve the group's own order when groupOrder is selected.
notes: Read browse capabilities first. Keep cursors and positional revisions with the query and viewer that produced them.

operations.title: Search the catalogue
operations.description: Searches visible titles, people, years and collections and returns grouped results. Each group previews up to 12 results; use its group and nextCursor to continue with up to 40 per page. Set record=1 only when a person commits a search.

params.q: Required search text, 1–128 Unicode characters after trimming and collapsing whitespace.
params.group: One result group: movies, shows, episodes, artists, albums, songs, books, collections, authors, people or live-tv. Use it with a continuation cursor; do not combine with groups.
params.groups: Comma-separated unique result groups: movies, shows, episodes, artists, albums, songs, books, collections, authors, people or live-tv. Omit to search all groups; do not combine with group.
params.cursor: Continuation returned for the selected group, at most 4096 characters; keep q, group, sort, direction, libraryIds and limit unchanged.
params.limit: Results per group, 1–40; defaults to 40 and larger values are capped at 40. Without group, each group shows at most 12 results.
params.sort: relevance (default), title, releaseYear or dateAdded. Artists, collections, authors, people and live-tv use title when releaseYear or dateAdded is requested.
params.direction: asc or desc. Defaults to asc for title and desc for relevance, releaseYear and dateAdded.
params.libraryIds: Comma-separated library IDs, at most 64, within the profile’s access; omit to search all visible libraries.
params.record: 0 (default) or 1. Use 1 only when a person commits a search; continuation requests do not record history.

operations.title: Read your search history
operations.description: Read searches saved for the current profile. Use it for recent-search suggestions rather than recording every keystroke.

operations.title: Clear your search history
operations.description: Clears the current current profile's saved search queries. It does not change other profiles' history.

operations.title: Find people
operations.description: Searches people in the visible catalogue. Use the returned person IDs to read credits and related titles.

params.limit: People per page, 1–100; defaults to 25.
params.q: Required search text, 1–128 Unicode characters after trimming and collapsing whitespace.

operations.title: Read a title
operations.description: Read one visible title with the current profile's personal state. Use its ID for detail, playback and personal-state requests.

operations.title: Read title details
operations.description: Build a title's detail screen from its details, files, metadata, personal state and available actions. Use related to request the supported related-content sections.

params.related: Set all to include related sections for episodes, songs and audiobook files. Movies include related sections by default; other title kinds have none.

operations.title: List title credits
operations.description: Look up a paged set of credits for a title. Use group to request the relevant credit group and continue with nextCursor.

params.cursor: Continuation returned by the previous page; send it unchanged with the same query.
params.group: Required credit group: cast or crew.
params.limit: Credits per page, 1–200; defaults to 200. Out-of-range values also use 200.

operations.title: List a show's seasons
operations.description: Find the visible seasons belonging to a show. Use their IDs to request episodes in season order.

operations.title: List a show's episodes
operations.description: Page through a show's episodes. Continue with the returned cursor rather than assuming a short page ends the list.

params.cursor: Continuation returned by the previous page; send it unchanged with the same query.
params.limit: Entries per page, 1–100; defaults to 40. Larger values are capped at 100.

operations.title: List a season's episodes
operations.description: Build a season's episode list from paged, visible entries. Use it to build an episode picker or a queue selector.

params.cursor: Continuation returned by the previous page; send it unchanged with the same query.
params.limit: Entries per page, 1–100; defaults to 40. Larger values are capped at 100.

operations.title: List an artist's albums
operations.description: Explore an artist's albums in pages. Follow nextCursor for additional albums.

params.cursor: Continuation returned by the previous page; send it unchanged with the same query.
params.limit: Entries per page, 1–100; defaults to 40. Larger values are capped at 100.

operations.title: List an album's songs
operations.description: Build an album's track list from paged songs. Keep the server's ordering when displaying the track list.

params.cursor: Continuation returned by the previous page; send it unchanged with the same query.
params.limit: Entries per page, 1–100; defaults to 40. Larger values are capped at 100.

operations.title: List an audiobook's chapters
operations.description: Page through an audiobook's chapters. Follow nextCursor to read the remaining chapter entries.

params.cursor: Continuation returned by the previous page; send it unchanged with the same query.
params.limit: Entries per page, 1–100; defaults to 40. Larger values are capped at 100.

operations.title: List an audiobook's files
operations.description: Find the visible files associated with an audiobook. Use the cursor to continue when the book spans more than one page.

params.cursor: Continuation returned by the previous page; send it unchanged with the same query.
params.limit: Entries per page, 1–100; defaults to 40. Larger values are capped at 100.

operations.title: Read a person's credits
operations.description: Read a person's catalogue page and paged credits. The role parameter narrows the credit view.

params.cursor: Continuation returned by the previous page; send it unchanged with the same query.
params.limit: Credits per page, 1–100; defaults to 40.

operations.title: Read a person's portrait
operations.description: Fetch the portrait image for a visible person. Use the URL supplied by catalogue responses.

params.v: Artwork version digest from the returned image URL.

operations.title: Read title artwork
operations.description: Fetch the selected image for a title and artwork kind. Replaced versioned images return 410; reuse the server's URL and validators.

params.kind: poster, backdrop, thumbnail, still, logo, square, portrait, banner or cover; use the returned artwork URL.
params.v: Artwork version digest from the returned image URL.
params.w: Artwork width from the returned URL: 400, 800 or 1920.

notes: The handler accepts w for the returned artwork sizes (400, 800 or 1920), though the spec omits that query parameter.

operations.title: Read entity artwork
operations.description: Fetch selected artwork for a title or supported container and role. Candidate previews require owner authority; use catalogue-provided URLs for ordinary artwork.

params.id: Entity ID for the requested kind.
params.role: poster, backdrop, thumbnail, still, logo, square, portrait, banner or cover; use the returned artwork URL.
params.candidate: Artwork candidate ID for an owner-only preview.
params.subject: Subject key from the returned artwork URL, at most 160 bytes; include it when the URL names a particular portrait.
params.v: Artwork version digest from the returned image URL.
params.w: Artwork width from the returned URL: 400, 800 or 1920.

notes: The handler accepts w for the returned artwork sizes (400, 800 or 1920), though the spec omits that query parameter.
operations.auth: A session or read-scoped API key or personal access token is required; only candidate previews require the owner.

operations.title: Read related title suggestions
operations.description: Find recommendations related to a visible title. Use these for a title's related-content section.

operations.title: Read related show suggestions
operations.description: Find recommendations related to a visible show. Visibility and content restrictions apply to the returned titles.

operations.title: Read lyrics choices
operations.description: Discover available lyrics resources, source information and the current profile's selection for a title. Use the returned resource and revision to fetch the lyrics document.

params.sessionId: Playback session whose source or presentation should be used.
params.sourceId: Exact media source ID from the lyrics source information.
params.sourceVersion: Exact source version from the lyrics source information.

operations.title: Read a lyrics document
operations.description: Fetch a particular revision of a lyrics resource for a visible title. Preserve the document's timing units when synchronizing lyrics with playback.

params.resource: Lyrics resource ID from the returned lyrics choices.
params.revision: Lyrics resource revision from the returned lyrics choices; keep it unchanged.
params.sessionId: Playback session whose source or presentation should be used.
params.sourceId: Exact media source ID from the lyrics source information.
params.sourceVersion: Exact source version from the lyrics source information.

operations.title: Choose a lyrics resource
operations.description: Saves the current profile's lyrics selection for the title. This changes personal playback state rather than replacing the shared lyrics resource.

operations.title: Read this device's playback capabilities
operations.description: Read the current device's capability document and revision. Keep its ETag for the next update; conditional reads can return 304.

operations.title: Publish this device's playback capabilities
operations.description: Replaces the device's supported engines, codecs, containers, subtitles and output limits. Send If-Match from the current document and declare only what the player can render. A missing `If-Match` returns 428; a stale revision returns 412.

params.If-Match: Current resource ETag or quoted revision from the preceding read.

notes: Send `If-Match`.

operations.title: Read playback choices for a title
operations.description: Choose playback for this device from the available sources, tracks, controls and delivery decision. Preview a particular version or quality before starting, then use the presentation engine selected by the server.

params.quality: original, automatic, fixed or limit; omit to use the saved quality choice. fixed requires qualityId; limit uses the numeric ceilings.
params.qualityId: Quality ladder ID from the delivery policy. Required for fixed; automatic accepts a ladder ID or original. Omit for original and limit.
params.maxVideoBitrateKbps: Video bitrate ceiling in kilobits per second, 0–2000000; use with quality=limit. 0 means no explicit ceiling.
params.maxHeight: Video height ceiling in pixels, 0–8640; use with quality=limit. 0 means no explicit ceiling.
params.maxAudioBitrateKbps: Audio bitrate ceiling in kilobits per second, 0–10000; use with quality=limit. 0 means no explicit ceiling.

operations.title: Read available playback qualities
operations.description: Check the delivery policy, quality ladder and saved quality choices available to clients. Use these values when presenting playback quality controls.

operations.title: Start playback
operations.description: Starts playback and returns a session and presentation URL with 201. A 202 means preparation is still running; follow Retry-After and replay the same request with the same Idempotency-Key.

params.Idempotency-Key: Stable request key; reuse it only with the identical request.

notes: A temporary conversion_capacity response uses 429 and Retry-After: 2. Retry the same request after that delay.
Send Idempotency-Key and reuse the same key and payload after a lost response.

operations.title: Read a playback session
operations.description: Read the session state, lease, revision and current presentation with its ETag. Reread it after a session.updated event or a revision conflict.

operations.title: Change playback
operations.description: Changes state, position, quality, version or tracks using If-Match. Changes to delivered bytes keep the session and queue but advance the presentation generation; adopt the new URLs.

params.If-Match: Current resource ETag or quoted revision from the preceding read.

notes: A temporary conversion_capacity response uses 429 and Retry-After: 2. Retry the same request after that delay.
Send `If-Match`.

operations.title: Report playback progress
operations.description: Reports the renderer's actual state and position using the current generation and a strictly increasing sequence. Reports renew the lease and update progress and history; serialize them and retry a lost response unchanged.

operations.title: Stop playback
operations.description: Stops the session and ends its playback grant access. The operation is idempotent and can include the final positionMs.

operations.title: Read playback chapters
operations.description: Build the active playback session's chapter list from paged entries. Keep the matching revision with chapter continuations and use the list for the player's chapter menu.

params.cursor: Continuation returned by the previous page; send it unchanged with the same query.
params.limit: Chapters per page, 1–100; defaults to 100.
params.revision: Chapter-list revision from the same playback session.

operations.title: List your devices' playback controls
operations.description: Check what the current profile is playing on its devices and which controls it may use. Page the list and use the returned session information for remote controls.

params.cursor: Continuation returned by the previous page; send it unchanged with the same query.
params.limit: Sessions per page, 1–100; defaults to 50.

operations.title: Read a title's source availability
operations.description: Check the advisory availability state of a visible title's sources. It does not select a source or grant playback access; use playback options and a session to play.

operations.title: Read seek preview information
operations.description: Discover available trickplay (seek preview) sets for a title. Use their returned URLs to show preview images while seeking.

operations.title: Read a seek preview index
operations.description: Map playback times to preview tiles with the WebVTT index. Fetch tiles using the URLs in the index.

params.set: Trickplay set identifier from the returned preview information.

operations.title: Read a seek preview tile
operations.description: Fetch one JPEG tile from a seek preview set after checking current title access. Conditional reads can reuse the image by ETag.

params.set: Trickplay set identifier from the returned preview information.
params.tile: Tile identifier from the returned trickplay index.
params.segment: Not accepted. This image handler rejects all query parameters; omit segment.

notes: Query parameters are rejected.

operations.title: Read a chapter image
operations.description: Fetch a thumbnail for a title's chapter after checking profile access. Use the returned image URL and its cache validator.

params.chapter: Chapter identifier from the title’s chapter information.
params.segment: Not accepted. This image handler rejects all query parameters; omit segment.

notes: Query parameters are rejected.

operations.title: Replace the device queue
operations.description: Replaces this device's queue from one selector form or a set of segments and can start the first session. Send Idempotency-Key and retain the returned queue revision.

params.Idempotency-Key: Stable request key; reuse it only with the identical request.

notes: A temporary conversion_capacity response uses 429 and Retry-After: 2. Retry the same request after that delay.
Send Idempotency-Key and reuse the same key and payload after a lost response.

operations.title: Read a queue

operations.title: Create a playlist
operations.description: Creates a playlist for the current profile using a client-generated `operationId` in the request body. Keep its ID and revision for later edits and queue selectors.
notes: For a new playlist, omit expectedRevision or send 0. A nonzero revision is rejected.
Reuse the client-generated `operationId` in the request body only when retrying the same request; use a new value for a new request.

operations.title: Read a playlist
operations.description: Read a playlist's name, summary, entry count, revision, sharing role and available actions. Browse its entries with a playlist group query.

operations.title: Edit a playlist
operations.description: Changes a playlist's supported fields using its expectedRevision and a client-generated `operationId` in the request body. Reread the resource when another edit changes the revision. Reconcile conflicts with the current state before retrying.
notes: Reuse the client-generated `operationId` in the request body only when retrying the same request; use a new value for a new request.

operations.title: Delete a playlist
operations.description: Deletes a playlist the current profile may manage using its `expectedRevision` and client-generated `operationId` in the request body. This removes the list rather than its library media. Reconcile conflicts with the current state before retrying.
notes: Reuse the client-generated `operationId` in the request body only when retrying the same request; use a new value for a new request.

operations.title: Add playlist entries
operations.description: Adds titles as playlist occurrences using a client-generated `operationId` in the request body and expectedRevision. An occurrence has its own entry ID, so a title can appear more than once. Reconcile conflicts with the current state before retrying.
notes: Reuse the client-generated `operationId` in the request body only when retrying the same request; use a new value for a new request.

operations.title: Remove a playlist entry
operations.description: Removes one playlist occurrence using its entry ID, expectedRevision and a client-generated `operationId` in the request body. Other occurrences of the same title remain. Reconcile conflicts with the current state before retrying.

params.entryId: Occurrence ID within the list or queue, not the title ID.

notes: Reuse the client-generated `operationId` in the request body only when retrying the same request; use a new value for a new request.

operations.title: Read playlist entry order
operations.description: Inspect a window of playlist entry IDs tied to the current revision, with pages of up to 100. Use entry IDs rather tha title IDs when reordering.

params.cursor: Continuation returned by the previous page; send it unchanged with the same query.
params.limit: Entry IDs per page, 1–100; defaults to 100.

operations.title: Reorder playlist entries
operations.description: Moves or permutes up to 200 occurrences using expectedRevision and a client-generated `operationId` in the request body. An afterEntryId places the selected block relative to an existing occurrence. Reconcile conflicts with the current state before retrying.
notes: Reuse the client-generated `operationId` in the request body only when retrying the same request; use a new value for a new request.

operations.title: List playlist sharing choices
operations.description: Returns a paged set of people the current profile may share this playlist with. Use these identities when changing shares.

params.cursor: Continuation returned by the previous page; send it unchanged with the same query.
params.limit: Sharing candidates per page, 1–100; defaults to 40.

operations.title: Share a playlist
operations.description: Adds or changes a playlist share for the named member or profile. Send the client-generated `operationId` in the request body and current expectedRevision and respect the caller's sharing role. Reconcile conflicts with the current state before retrying.
notes: Reuse the client-generated `operationId` in the request body only when retrying the same request; use a new value for a new request.

operations.title: Remove a playlist share
operations.description: Removes the specified share using a client-generated `operationId` in the request body and expectedRevision. The playlist remains available to its other permitted viewers. Reconcile conflicts with the current state before retrying.
notes: Reuse the client-generated `operationId` in the request body only when retrying the same request; use a new value for a new request.

operations.title: List saved resources
operations.description: Returns the current profile’s saved collections or saved filters, selected by the required kind. Set pinned=true to read only pinned resources in the current profile’s arrangement.

params.cursor: Continuation returned by the previous page; send it unchanged with the same query.
params.pinned: true or 1 returns only pinned resources in the profile’s arrangement. false, 0 or omission includes both pinned and unpinned resources.
params.limit: Resources per page, 1–100; defaults to 40.

notes: The handler accepts limit (1–100, default 40) even though this spec operation omits it.

operations.title: Read a saved resource
operations.description: Returns a saved resource's definition, status, revision, sharing role and available actions. Use its group in structured browse to read its titles.

operations.title: Create a saved resource
operations.description: Creates a supported personal collection or saved filter using a client-generated `operationId` in the request body and expectedRevision. Keep the returned definition and revision for later changes.
notes: For a new resource, send expectedRevision: 0 with kind collection or view. A saved view also needs its query definition.
Reuse the client-generated `operationId` in the request body only when retrying the same request; use a new value for a new request.

operations.title: Edit a saved resource
operations.description: Changes a saved resource's name, summary or supported definition fields. Send expectedRevision and a client-generated `operationId` in the request body to protect concurrent edits. Reconcile conflicts with the current state before retrying.
notes: Reuse the client-generated `operationId` in the request body only when retrying the same request; use a new value for a new request.

operations.title: Delete a saved resource
operations.description: Deletes a saved resource the current profile may manage using expectedRevision and a client-generated `operationId` in the request body. Its library titles are retained. Reconcile conflicts with the current state before retrying.
notes: Reuse the client-generated `operationId` in the request body only when retrying the same request; use a new value for a new request.

operations.title: Change collection membership
operations.description: Adds titles to or removes entries from a personal collection using expectedRevision and a client-generated `operationId` in the request body. Inspect per-entry outcomes because hidden or missing titles can be refused individually. Reconcile conflicts with the current state before retrying.
notes: Reuse the client-generated `operationId` in the request body only when retrying the same request; use a new value for a new request.

operations.title: Reorder a personal collection
operations.description: Moves up to 200 entries in a personal collection using its `expectedRevision` and a client-generated `operationId` in the request body. Send entryIds in the desired order. Set afterEntryId to move them after that entry, or to an empty string to move them to the front; omit it to rearrange only their existing positions. Reconcile conflicts with the current state before retrying.
notes: Reuse the client-generated `operationId` in the request body only when retrying the same request; use a new value for a new request.

operations.title: List saved-resource sharing choices
operations.description: Returns people the current profile may share this saved resource with. Continue with its cursor when more candidates are available.

params.cursor: Continuation returned by the previous page; send it unchanged with the same query.

operations.title: Share a saved resource
operations.description: Adds or changes access for the named member or profile. Send expectedRevision and a client-generated `operationId` in the request body and use an allowed sharing role. Reconcile conflicts with the current state before retrying.
notes: Reuse the client-generated `operationId` in the request body only when retrying the same request; use a new value for a new request.

operations.title: Remove a saved-resource share
operations.description: Removes the specified share using expectedRevision and a client-generated `operationId` in the request body. Other shares and the saved resource remain. Reconcile conflicts with the current state before retrying.
notes: Reuse the client-generated `operationId` in the request body only when retrying the same request; use a new value for a new request.

operations.title: List visible TV sources
operations.description: Find the Live TV sources available to the current profile. Use their IDs to narrow the guide and channel directory.

params.includeHidden: true or false (default). Only the owner may set true to include channels hidden by the viewer; other callers receive 403.
params.timezone: IANA time zone name, such as America/Halifax; omit for UTC.

operations.title: Browse TV channels
operations.description: Browse the channel directory with its supported sort, filters and positioning information. Keep its revision when continuing a positional or anchored window.

params.anchorChannelId: Channel ID used to anchor a directory window.
params.anchorProvenance: live-source or library-channel; required with direction.
params.anchorSourceId: Source ID of the channel used as the directory anchor.
params.direction: next or previous relative to anchorChannelId, anchorSourceId and anchorProvenance. Omit offset; omit limit or set it to 1. Omit direction for an ordinary directory window.
params.favorites: true or false (default); true returns only this profile’s favourite channels.
params.group: Exact channel group name, at most 120 bytes; omit to include all groups.
params.includeHidden: true or false (default). Only the owner may set true to include channels hidden by the viewer; other callers receive 403.
params.limit: Channels per window, 1–50; defaults to 50. With direction, omit limit or set it to 1.
params.offset: Zero-based directory offset, 0–3200064; defaults to 0. Omit when direction is set.
params.revision: Directory revision, at most 64 bytes; retain it when continuing a window.
params.search: Text to match channel names or groups, at most 120 bytes.
params.sourceId: Source ID to filter channels, at most 256 bytes; omit to include all visible sources.
params.timezone: IANA time zone name, such as America/Halifax; omit for UTC.

operations.title: Read the TV guide
operations.description: Read channels and programs for a time range under the current profile’s source access. Use RFC 3339 timestamps with whole seconds and continue with the returned paging information.

params.cursor: Continuation returned by the previous page; send it unchanged with the same query.
params.end: Required guide-window end as RFC 3339 with whole seconds, after start and no more than 24 hours later.
params.favorites: true or false (default); true returns only this profile’s favourite channels.
params.group: Exact channel group name, at most 120 bytes; omit to include all groups.
params.includeHidden: true or false (default); true includes channels this profile has hidden.
params.kind: Required: live-source or library-channel. Omission and all are rejected.
params.limit: Required channels per page, 1–50.
params.programmes: Set `programmes=none` for channels only; leave it out to include program data.
params.search: Text to match channel names or groups, at most 120 bytes.
params.sourceId: Source ID to filter channels; omit to include all visible sources.
params.start: Required guide-window start as RFC 3339 with whole seconds; end must follow it by at most 24 hours.
params.timezone: IANA time zone name, such as America/Halifax; omit for UTC.

notes: Send `start`, `end` and `limit`.

operations.title: Read a TV program image
operations.description: Fetch an image for a program in the named guide generation. Use the image URL returned by the guide.

params.generation: Generation from the current presentation or guide image URL.
params.programme: TV program identifier from the guide image URL.

operations.title: Change channel preferences
operations.description: Sets the current profile's favourite or hidden state for a source channel. Send the request ID and expectedRevision from the current channel preferences. Reconcile conflicts with the current state before retrying.

operations.title: Change library-channel preferences
operations.description: Sets the current profile's favourite or hidden state for a library channel. Send the request ID and current expectedRevision. Reconcile conflicts with the current state before retrying.

operations.title: Read a library-channel logo
operations.description: Returns the image for a visible channel generated from library titles. Use the logo URL provided by the channel response.

operations.title: Read a Live TV media resource
operations.description: Delivers a media resource for the current linear playback generation and token. Use the URLs returned by a channel playback presentation.

params.playbackId: Linear playback ID from the current presentation URL.
params.generation: Generation from the current presentation or guide image URL.
params.token: Secret token component from the current Live TV presentation URL.
params.name: Media resource name from the current Live TV presentation.

operations.auth: The token in the returned presentation URL authorizes the request; no Authorization header is needed.

operations.title: List recordings
operations.description: Find recordings for the current profile in pages filtered by state. The default state is upcoming; continue with the returned cursor.

params.cursor: Continuation returned by the previous page; send it unchanged with the same query.
params.limit: Recordings per page, 1–50; defaults to 50.
params.state: upcoming (default), recorded, history, rules or all.

operations.title: List recording channel choices
operations.description: Find channels available to the current profile for recording. Narrow by source or search and continue with the cursor.

params.cursor: Continuation returned by the previous page; send it unchanged with the same query.
params.sourceId: Live TV source ID to restrict the recording channel choices.

operations.title: Schedule a recording
operations.description: Schedules a program occurrence with a stable requestId and supplied or default options. Recording access and available capture support are checked by the server.

operations.title: Read a recording
operations.description: Read one visible recording and its current actions, revision and overlapping recordings. Continue overlaps using nextOverlap as after.

params.after: Recording ID from nextOverlap to continue the overlap list, 20 entries at a time; omit for the first page.

operations.title: Change recording options
operations.description: Updates a recording using the request's `expectedRevision` precondition. Reread after dvr_conflict before applying a new edit.

operations.title: Cancel a recording
operations.description: Cancels a recording using the current `expectedRevision` and request ID. Use the action offered by the recording's current state. Reconcile conflicts with the current state before retrying.

operations.title: Change recording retention
operations.description: Changes the recording's keep setting using its current `expectedRevision` and request ID. This controls whether ordinary recording cleanup may remove it. Reconcile conflicts with the current state before retrying.

operations.title: Preview recording deletion
operations.description: Returns the effect of deleting a recording before the current profile confirms it. Read the current recording and preview before sending a delete.

operations.title: Delete a recording
operations.description: Deletes a recording the current profile may manage using its `expectedRevision` and request ID. Use the preview to show the effect before submitting. Reconcile conflicts with the current state before retrying.

operations.title: Preview a recording rule
operations.description: Evaluates a proposed recording rule before it is saved. Use the returned matches to check that the rule selects the intended programs.

operations.title: Save a recording rule
operations.description: Creates or updates a recording rule with its revision precondition. The body's ID must match the rule ID in the path.
notes: Send expectedRevision: 0 to create a rule, or the current rule revision to update it; reconcile conflicts before retrying.

operations.title: Delete a recording rule
operations.description: Removes a recording rule using the request's `expectedRevision` and identity fields. Reconcile a conflict before repeating the edit.

operations.title: Follow resource changes
operations.description: Streams authorized invalidation hints as SSE, or returns JSON when waitMs is supplied. Resume SSE with Last-Event-ID or polling with nextAfter; stream.resync means reread visible resources and continue from the new position.

params.after: Position from nextAfter for JSON polling with waitMs. For SSE, resume with Last-Event-ID instead; an after query parameter is rejected.
params.waitMs: Use 0–25000 milliseconds for a JSON event poll; omit for SSE.

notes: One installation shares one SSE stream. Refresh credentials and reconnect at the token deadline or when the stream ends.
Treat events as hints to reread resources, not as a complete change log; retain positions even for filtered events.

operations.title: Read notification options
operations.description: Check the notification features and actions available to the current profile. Use them before presenting inbox controls.

operations.title: Read the notification inbox
operations.description: Page through the inbox with its own revision, filtered by audience and state. Keep the scope and revision from the returned data envelope.

params.audience: all (default), profile or account-admin. account-admin requires the local owner; all includes only audiences the caller can read.
params.cursor: Continuation returned by the previous page; send it unchanged with the same query.
params.limit: Notifications per page, 1–100; defaults to 40.

operations.title: Read the unread notification count
operations.description: Check the unread count for the selected audience. Refresh it after notification.changed rather than deriving it from event positions.

params.audience: all (default), profile or account-admin. account-admin requires the local owner; all includes only audiences the caller can read.

operations.title: Change notification state
operations.description: Applies read or archive actions with a client-generated `operationId` in the request body and expectedRevision. Use the inbox revision, which is independent of the event feed cursor. Reconcile conflicts with the current state before retrying.
notes: Reuse the client-generated `operationId` in the request body only when retrying the same request; use a new value for a new request.

operations.title: Query titles or provider IDs
operations.description: Lists one title kind in one library or finds a title by provider and providerId. Pages default to 50 and allow 1–100; cursors last 30 minutes and can finish a walk during a scan.

params.library: Library ID; required for a title list and optional for provider lookup.
params.kind: movie, show, season, episode, artist, album, song, book, author or collection.
params.order: Title-query direction: asc or desc; defaults to asc.
params.yearFrom: Earliest year, inclusive; use only with sort=year.
params.yearTo: Latest year, inclusive; use only with sort=year.
params.addedAfter: Include titles added after this RFC 3339 time; use only with sort=added.
params.addedBefore: Include titles added before this RFC 3339 time; use only with sort=added.
params.provider: Provider for an ID lookup: tmdb, tvdb, imdb or anilist.
params.providerId: Title ID at the named metadata provider; use with provider.
params.cursor: Continuation returned by the previous page; send it unchanged with the same query.
params.limit: Titles per page, 1–100; defaults to 50.

notes: Ranges are accepted only on the selected sort key. Reconcile an index by stable title ID when concurrent edits move sort keys.

operations.title: Report changed files or folders
operations.description: Accepts up to 200 absolute paths as the server sees them and queues scans of the affected folders. A 202 includes per-path status; outside_libraries means that path did not schedule work.
notes: Map paths to the server’s filesystem before sending them. Inspect each path’s status even when HTTP returns 202.
Requires the owner.

operations.title: Start a library scan
operations.description: Queues an incremental, full or integrity scan for a library and returns 202. If a scan is already running, the server returns that scan; use changed paths when only particular folders changed.

params.mode: Scan mode: incremental, full or integrity.

notes: A 202 receipt or running job does not establish that the scan finished. Poll the job or check scan.finished webhooks.
Requires the owner.

operations.title: Read library scan status
operations.description: Check the library's current inventory and scan status, including progress and completed source scans. Players and tools can read it without owner-only job access.

operations.title: List scan jobs
operations.description: Review scan job history for an owner integration. Use the returned jobs and continuation information to follow recent ingestion work.

params.libraryId: Library ID used to narrow scan jobs.
params.status: queued, running, paused, complete, complete_with_warnings, failed or cancelled; omit to include all states.
params.limit: Jobs per page, 1–40; defaults to 40.
params.cursor: Continuation from the preceding scan-job page.

notes: The handler accepts libraryId, status, limit (1–40) and cursor even though this spec operation omits those query parameters.

operations.title: Read a scan job
operations.description: Track the current status, phase, processed counts and warnings for an ingestion job. A 202 response or a queued or running job does not prove that the scan finished or that imported files are ready.
notes: Poll the job or check `scan.finished` webhooks to confirm that the scan finished.
Requires the owner.

operations.title: Cancel a scan job
operations.description: Requests cancellation of an ingestion job for the owner. Read the job again to reconcile its final outcome.

operations.title: Read skipped scan entries
operations.description: Inspect files and folders skipped by a scan, paged by sequence. Limit defaults to 64 and allows up to 128.

params.after: Sequence after which to read skipped entries.
params.limit: Entries per page, 1–128; defaults to 64.

notes: Requires the owner.

operations.title: Read source inventory changes
operations.description: Read retained inventory changes for one library source after a sequence. Handle the returned cursor-expiry information by rebuilding the affected inventory.

params.after: Retained inventory sequence after which to read changes.

notes: Requires the owner.

operations.title: Read library inventory entries
operations.description: Inspect paged inventory entries for an owner integration, with filters for source, asset or state. Use it to investigate unmatched or unavailable files.

params.sourceId: Library source ID to restrict the inventory entries.
params.assetId: Inventory asset ID used to narrow the results.
params.state: available, missing or unsupported; omit to include all states.
params.cursor: Continuation returned by the previous page; send it unchanged with the same query.
params.limit: Inventory entries per page, 1–40; defaults to 40.

operations.title: Read an entity's match and metadata
operations.description: Inspect the repair state, current revision, match evidence and provider candidates for a supported entity kind. Read this before searching for or selecting a different match.

params.id: Entity ID for the requested kind.

notes: Requires the owner.

operations.title: Change an entity's match and metadata
operations.description: Applies a metadata repair action, including searching, choosing a provider candidate or editing fields. Send the current expectedRevision and any required confirmation; provider work can continue in the background. Reconcile conflicts with the current state before retrying.

params.id: Entity ID for the requested kind.

notes: Requires the owner.
For cancel_cascade, operationId in the request body is the existing server-generated cascade ID from the repair state, not a client-generated idempotency value.

operations.title: List a library's titles that need attention
operations.description: Read unmatched and uncertain titles with their best candidates from the library’s Needs attention queue. Pages default to 25 and allow 1–50; includeInProgress controls whether work already running is listed.

params.cursor: Continuation returned by the previous page; send it unchanged with the same query.
params.limit: Titles per page, 1–50; defaults to 25.
params.includeInProgress: Whether to include titles whose metadata work is already running; defaults to true.

notes: Requires the owner.

operations.title: List titles that need attention across libraries
operations.description: Page through unmatched and uncertain titles in the server’s Needs attention queue. Use it for a metadata integration’s review work.

params.cursor: Continuation returned by the previous page; send it unchanged with the same query.
params.limit: Titles per page, 1–50; defaults to 25.
params.includeInProgress: Whether to include titles whose metadata work is already running; defaults to true.

notes: Requires the owner.

operations.title: Count titles that need attention
operations.description: Read counts for each library’s Needs attention queue and the server total. Use them for an integration dashboard without fetching every uncertain title.
notes: Requires the owner.

operations.title: Resolve a title that needs attention
operations.description: Accepts a candidate, searches, enters a provider ID or dismisses a title from the library’s Needs attention queue. Send the command’s current `expectedRevision` and inspect the accepted work after the 202 receipt. Reconcile conflicts with the current state before retrying.
notes: Requires the owner.

operations.title: Refresh a title's metadata
operations.description: Queues a fresh metadata fetch for the title and returns 202. Reread its details or match state after the background work finishes.
notes: Requires the owner.

operations.title: Refresh a show's metadata
operations.description: Queues a fresh metadata fetch for the show and returns 202. Existing metadata remains readable while the work runs.
notes: Requires the owner.

operations.title: Read editable title metadata
operations.description: Read manually editable title metadata and its revision for the owner. Use this read before applying field changes.

operations.title: Edit title metadata
operations.description: Lets the owner change manually editable metadata fields. Send the current `expectedRevision` and reconcile manual_metadata_conflict before retrying.

operations.title: List active playback sessions
operations.description: Monitor a paged list of active sessions with the profile, title, device and delivery information. Refresh it after an admin.sessions event to keep a dashboard current.

params.limit: Sessions per page, 1–200; defaults to 50.
params.cursor: Continuation returned by the previous page; send it unchanged with the same query.

notes: Requires the member to have administrator playback permission.

operations.title: Read an active session's controls
operations.description: Check the controls an administrator can use for a playback session and the current control revision. Read it before submitting an administrative control.
notes: Requires the member to have administrator playback permission.

operations.title: Control an active session
operations.description: Applies an allowed playback action with expectedRevision and a position for seek where needed. Use the controls resource to check what the administrator may do. Reconcile conflicts with the current state before retrying.
notes: Requires the member to have administrator playback permission.

operations.title: End an active playback session
operations.description: Ends a viewer's playback and can show an optional message to them. The operation is idempotent.
notes: Requires the member to have administrator playback permission.

operations.title: List webhooks and event types
operations.description: Review configured webhooks and the event types available for subscriptions. Secrets are represented by hints.
notes: Requires the owner.

operations.title: Create a webhook
operations.description: Adds a destination and event subscription and returns its signing secret once. URLs may use HTTP or HTTPS, including a private network address, but cannot contain a username or password.
notes: Keep the signing secret privately; it is shown only when issued or replaced.
Requires the owner.

operations.title: Read a webhook
operations.description: Inspect one webhook's configuration, revision and delivery state. Read it before changing a subscription.
notes: Requires the owner.

operations.title: Change a webhook
operations.description: Changes the destination, events or enabled state using expectedRevision. Setting rotateSecret returns the replacement signing secret once; disabling a webhook abandons queued deliveries. Reconcile conflicts with the current state before retrying.
notes: Keep the signing secret privately; it is shown only when issued or replaced.
Requires the owner.

operations.title: Delete a webhook
operations.description: Removes the webhook together with its waiting deliveries and delivery log. Use this when an integration is disconnected.
notes: Requires the owner.

operations.title: Send a webhook test
operations.description: Queues a webhook.test event even if the webhook is disabled and returns 202. Check the delivery log to confirm that the receiver accepted it.
notes: Requires the owner.

operations.title: Read webhook delivery results
operations.description: Review a paged delivery log, newest first, with attempt counts and HTTP results. Event IDs stay the same across retries so receivers can ignore duplicate deliveries.

params.cursor: Continuation returned by the previous page; send it unchanged with the same query.
params.limit: Deliveries per page, 1–100; defaults to 50.

notes: Verify signatures against the raw request body, reject stale timestamps and deduplicate Portico-Event-Id values at the receiver.
Requires the owner.

operations.title: Call the MCP server
operations.description: Accepts MCP JSON-RPC over stateless Streamable HTTP, with JSON responses and no session ID to retain. Use initialize, tools/list and tools/call with an API key or personal access token; signed-in app sessions are refused.
notes: Use an API key or personal access token with the scopes needed by the requested tools.
POST supports initialize, ping, tools/list, tools/call and notifications. GET returns 405; there is no server event stream.
Supported protocol versions: 2025-06-18, 2025-03-26 and 2024-11-05. Tools are filtered by scope, role and configured features.
operations.auth: API key or personal access token required; app sessions aren't accepted.
